title: reorganize-artifacts-and-introduce-sparse-test-reloader
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Reorganize build artifact layout for clearer downstream consumption; add sparse test reloader to reduce CI flakiness and cost; update dependency refresh rules to ignore workspace devDeps; refactor lint/test pipelines to staged-runner and caching.
body:
Motivation: Our CI pipeline has grown noisy and expensive due to wide integration test runs on small repo changes and a non-deterministic artifact layout that complicates downstream release steps. This PR reorganizes where build artifacts land, centralizes artifact metadata, and introduces a sparse test reloader that only re-runs affected test subsets in presubmit and nightly lanes. It also tightens the dep-refresh bot to avoid creating churn from devDependencies across monorepo workspaces.

Summary of changes: 1) artifact layout: /artifacts/{component}/{os}/{arch}/{commit} with a lightweight metadata.json describing checksums and component provenance; 2) sparse test reloader: a new service (scripts/ci/sparse_test_reloader.py) plus test-mapping metadata generated during build to map changed files to test groups; 3) staged-runner: split lint and test into fast lint -> unit -> integration stages with explicit cache priming and a new composite GitHub Action (.github/actions/staged-runner) to coordinate stage transitions; 4) dependency refresh rules: update .github/dependabot.yaml to exclude devDeps for workspace packages and add a small heuristic to group non-breaking upgrades; 5) release automation: update .github/workflows/release.yml to consume new artifact layout and verify metadata.json signatures before publishing.

Why this is different from previous CI work: instead of slicing by language only, the sparse test reloader uses per-component change maps generated at build time so we avoid running unrelated integration suites. The artifact layout replaces ad-hoc tarball names with a deterministic, machine-readable structure which simplifies signing, caching, and mirrors.

Checklist:
- [x] Artifact layout implemented and backwards-compatible reader in release job
- [x] Sparse test reloader integrated into presubmit lanes (fast-path)
- [x] Staged-runner action added and adopted by top-level workflows
- [x] Dependabot config tightened and tested against a dry-run
- [x] Manual verification of release job consuming new layout
- [x] Documentation: docs/dev/ci-artifacts.md and docs/dev/sparse-tests.md added

Commits (high level):
- feat(ci): introduce deterministic artifact layout and metadata.json
- feat(ci): add sparse test reloader + test mapping generator
- chore(ci): composite action staged-runner and action inputs
- perf(ci): cache priming hooks for staged-runner
- chore(deps): update dependabot rules to skip workspace devDeps
- docs: add CI artifact and sparse test documentation

Files changed (high level):
- .github/workflows/build.yml (refactored to emit artifact metadata and call staged-runner)
- .github/workflows/release.yml (consume new layout + verify signatures)
- .github/dependabot.yaml (refine ignore rules for devDeps and workspace packages)
- .github/actions/staged-runner/action.yml (+entrypoint scripts)
- scripts/ci/sparse_test_reloader.py (new)
- scripts/ci/generate_test_map.py (new)
- tooling/artifact/packager.go (write metadata.json)
- docs/dev/ci-artifacts.md (new)
- docs/dev/sparse-tests.md (new)
- package.json / yarn.lock (touched: test-mapping helper in js workspace)
- Makefile (top-level: add `ci-artifacts` target)

Review conversation (abridged):
- Maya Singh (requested changes): "This looks great; two asks: 1) ensure the artifact metadata includes the builder image hash for reproducibility, and 2) don't change release.yml behavior for v1.0 maintenance branch. Please add tests for metadata consumer."
- Priya Nair (author): "Added builder image hash and added a compatibility check in release.yml that falls back to legacy layout when a release metadata tag exists. Unit test for metadata consumer added in tooling/artifact/packager_test.go."
- Evan Liu (comment): "Sparse reloader is promising; worried about mapping correctness for generated code. Suggest adding a conservative fallback to run full suite if mapping is empty or ambiguous."
- Priya Nair: "Added fallback: if test-map returns empty or marked ambiguous we mark job as 'run-all' and emit a debug artifact; updated docs with mapping caveats."
- Carlos Rivera (approval): "Verified staged-runner reduces median presubmit runtime by ~28% in our sample. Approving."

CI timeline and checks: initial run failed due to cache key mismatch in staged-runner (action input change). I updated the action inputs and retriggered. Second run: lint/unit/integration all passed. Dependabot dry-run against a test repo showed expected behavior. Release workflow dry-run verified reading metadata.json and rejecting signatures that do not match recorded builder hash. Final CI status: pass.

Merge outcome: squash-merged to main on 2026-01-22 after approvals. Included a short merge commit message: "reorganize artifacts; add sparse test reloader; staged-runner action; tighten dependabot".

Follow-ups (tracked separately):
- ENG-3380: expand sparse test map heuristics to include generated protobufs and codegen pipelines (medium priority).
- ENG-3421: add a cached artifact mirror in S3 for cross-region release performance (low priority).
- ENG-3499: instrument sparse reloader telemetry (counts of fallback-to-full-run) and alert on spike.

Notes for maintainers:
- Backwards compatibility: release job will check for legacy artifact names and prefer them only for branches with metadata v0 markers. The compatibility shim is intentionally conservative; we'll schedule a migration window and notify integrators via #infra-dev.
- Security: metadata.json is signed by the builder key in CI; maintainers should rotate builder keys via the documented KMS rotation process.

If you want to reproduce locally: see docs/dev/ci-artifacts.md for the sample packager invocation and docs/dev/sparse-tests.md for using generate_test_map.py against a local checkout.
